This name, derived from the Sanskrit word 'mohana', evokes the rich imagery of the Indian landscape. In Hindu mythology, mountains are considered sacred as they are believed to be the abode of various gods and goddesses. The name Mohana, which means mountain or hill, takes its inspiration from this cultural belief and represents a connection to the rich and diverse Indian heritage.

In Hindu mythology, the god Vishnu is often depicted as reclining on a mountain, symbolizing his divine presence and sustenance of the universe. Flowers are also considered sacred in Hinduism, representing the divine presence. Thus, the name Mohana combines the imagery of the mountain and the flowers, evoking a sense of peace, serenity, and spiritual connection. The name Mohana acts as a gentle reminder of the eternal and divine presence within us all.

historical_references.reference: Mohana, a king mentioned in the Mahabharata, was the ruler of the Vidarbha kingdom. He was a friend and ally of the Pandava brothers, and played a significant role in the Mahabharata war.

Mohana was also a popular name for Jain monks during the 11th and 12th centuries. One such monk, Mohana Suri, was an influential figure in the Digambara sect of Jainism and contributed significantly to the development of Jain philosophy and literature.
